headline: High: Roo Code’s default filesystem/MCP/network access can leak or corrupt Dexter’s financial-research outputs when paired in the same workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dexter writes scratchpad files and uses autonomous execution, while Roo Code reads/writes the VS Code workspace and can use MCP. If Dexter’s outputs are placed in shared files, Roo Code may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. This is a plausible shared-channel pathway, but not proven by direct pair evidence.
conditions: IF Dexter writes untrusted content into .dexter/scratchpad/ that Roo Code reads
IF Roo Code is configured to ingest workspace files or MCP outputs as instructions
mitigations: Separate Dexter scratchpad and Roo workspace directories
Disable MCP servers for the Roo session
Mark workspace files from Dexter as data-only in operator workflow
Add a manual review step before Roo acts on Dexter-generated text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter handles financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API keys; Roo Code can read workspace files and also has broad egress. In a shared workspace, sensitive Dexter artifacts can flow into Roo Code and then out through model or MCP calls. The pairwise leakage path is credible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace containing financial data or secrets
IF Roo Code sends workspace contents to a configured model API or MCP server
mitigations: Keep financial data outside the shared VS Code workspace
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent
Remove API keys from files accessible to Roo Code
Disable network egress for Roo Code during Dexter runs
Restrict Dexter outputs to redacted summaries only

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter supports multiple instances and Roo Code shares state via filesystem while also writing and modifying git state. Both can operate on the same workspace, so concurrent writes and git mutations can collide without locking. The overlap is directly supported by both profiles.
conditions: IF Dexter instances and Roo Code target the same directory
IF both agents modify the same files or git branch without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate workspace clone
Pause one agent before the other edits git state
Use branch-per-agent workflow
Enable file locking or serialized task execution
Review git diffs before any commit

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter produces autonomous research outputs, and Roo Code can act on workspace content with shell, git, and browser tools. If Roo Code treats Dexter’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect code changes or external actions. The pathway exists, but Roo Code’s approval-per-tool default reduces severity below high.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes Dexter-generated findings without verification
IF Roo Code uses those findings to edit code, commit git changes, or browse/act externally
mitigations: Require a human check before Roo acts on Dexter outputs
Ask Roo to cite source files before making changes
Use a verification checklist for Dexter-generated claims
Limit Roo to read-only review mode for Dexter artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly touches financial data and market data, while Roo Code can read workspace files and send them to configured model APIs or MCP servers. If regulated financial data or secrets are present, the pair can move them into third-party services without a documented residency or retention boundary. The profiles do not show a mitigating compliance control.
conditions: IF regulated financial data or secrets are stored in the shared workspace
IF Roo Code forwards those files to an external model API or MCP server
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Roo Code’s workspace
Use a local-only model for Roo Code when handling sensitive files
Redact secrets before either agent processes the files
Document retention and residency for all configured APIs
Run a compliance review before enabling shared access
